steps.say: Each turn starts with an opening card. You and SAE each pick one in secret, then both are shown together. An opening card is used only for its event: its action points are not spent. Pick Maastricht Treaty.

SAE picked Handover of Hong Kong. The card with more action points goes first: Hong Kong has 4 and Maastricht 2, so SAE's event happens first. On a tie, LIO's pick would go first, whichever side's card it is.

Maastricht gives you {eventPoints:e1-lio-001} point now. You can place where you already have influence ({influenceIn:lio}), next to it, or next to the United States ({homeNeighbours:lio}). For the rest of this turn, each time you spend points, you spend 1 more.

variants.say: Maastricht gives you {eventPoints:e1-lio-001} point now. You can place next to the United States ({homeNeighbours:lio}). For the rest of this turn, each time you spend points, you spend 1 more.

steps.say: Now the card plays: LIO, SAE, LIO, SAE. Play NATO Enlargement 1999 for its points: 3, plus 1 from Maastricht, so {cardPoints:e1-lio-004} to spend. All of a play's points go to one action.

You control a country when your influence there is at least its stability, and at least SAE's influence plus its stability. Mexico has stability 2: 2 influence controls it. Placing in a country SAE controls costs 2 points for each influence. Where you can place is fixed when the play starts.
Primakov's U-turn is SAE's card. You can play it only for its points, and its event still happens, as SAE's event.

You choose whether the event comes before or after you spend. It makes you spend 1 fewer for the rest of the turn. Before: 1, plus 1 from Maastricht, minus 1, gives {pointsBefore:e1-sae-008} point. After: you spend {pointsAfter:e1-sae-008}, and the penalty only reaches spends later this turn, when you have no plays left. Chapter 6 shows the one exception: points spent on the tech race cancel the event.

variants.say: You choose whether the event comes before or after you spend. It makes you spend 1 fewer for the rest of the turn. Before: 1, plus 1 from Maastricht, minus 1, minus {modifierTakesOff:e1-neu-001} from Rwandan Genocide, and never below 1, gives {pointsBefore:e1-sae-008} point. After: you also spend {pointsAfter:e1-sae-008}, so here the order doesn't change your points, and the penalty only reaches spends later this turn, when you have no plays left. Chapter 6 shows the one exception: points spent on the tech race cancel the event.

steps.say: Turn 2: both hands fill back up to 8. Pick Partnership for Peace, and keep Desert Storm Coalition, Budapest Memorandum and Second Chechen War for the next chapters.
Play Desert Storm Coalition for its {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points and intervene in any country where SAE has influence. It doesn't need to be next to yours.

There are no dice: you draw a card numbered 1 to 6 from your Contingency deck. Result = draw + points spent - 2 x the country's stability. If the result is above 0, SAE loses that much influence there, and what is left over becomes yours. With {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points, a stability-2 country such as Crimea gives a result equal to your draw. An intervention in a battleground raises Escalation by 1.

If the result is above 0, SAE loses that much influence there, and what is left over becomes yours. With {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points, a stability-2 country such as Crimea gives a result {belowDraw:e1-lio-006} below your draw. An intervention in a battleground raises Escalation by 1.

If the result is above 0, SAE loses that much influence there, and what is left over becomes yours. With {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points, a stability-2 country such as Crimea gives a result {aboveDraw:e1-lio-006} above your draw. An intervention in a battleground raises Escalation by 1.

steps.say: Both sides see every draw. A used card stays out until the deck is reshuffled, when two are left, so a low draw now means higher ones are still to come.

say: Escalation runs from 0 to 6. At 3, Eastern Europe and Central Asia closes to interventions and realignments. At 4, East and South Asia closes as well, and at 5, Europe. Placing is never blocked. Escalation falls by 1 at each turn's end. At 6 there is a crisis: whoever caused it draws from their deck, loses that much score, and Escalation drops back to 3.
Play Budapest Memorandum for its {cardPoints:e1-lio-002} points and realign: each point is one attempt, on a country where SAE has influence, in a region that is still open.

steps.say: Both sides draw. Each side adds 1 for each neighbouring country it controls, 1 if it has more influence there, and 1 if its home box touches the country. The higher total wins, and the loser loses the difference in influence. A tie changes nothing, and you may stop early. Next to Russia or China, SAE's home box gives it +1.
Turn 3, the last of Era 1. Pick Arrest of Aldrich Ames: its event shows you SAE's hand.

Play Second Chechen War, SAE's card, on the tech race. Played any other way, its event would give SAE {eventPoints:e1-sae-004} points and raise Escalation. Points spent on the tech race cancel a rival card's event.

variants.say: Your {cardPoints:e1-sae-004} point can't pay this step's cost of {techRaceCost:lio} this turn. Play Second Chechen War for its points and place influence instead: its event, SAE's, still happens. Played this way, its event gives SAE {eventPoints:e1-sae-004} points and raises Escalation. Points spent on the tech race would have cancelled it.

steps.say: One shared marker starts at parity. Moving it toward your side costs 1 for Networks and Orbit, 2 for AI, 3 for Hypersonics and 4 for Quantum Computing. Pulling SAE's lead back costs what SAE's step cost. All {cardPoints:e1-sae-004} points go to this one try, so any above the cost are lost. Draw: on 4 or more, the marker moves one step. Each side may try once per turn.

One shared marker starts at parity. Moving it toward your side costs 1 for Networks and Orbit, 2 for AI, 3 for Hypersonics and 4 for Quantum Computing. Pulling SAE's lead back costs what SAE's step cost. Your 1 point goes to this one try. Draw: on 4 or more, the marker moves one step. Each side may try once per turn.

steps.say: While the marker is on your side, you hold its step and every step below it. Networks and Orbit gives +1 in your realignments, and AI gives +1 on your interventions. Hypersonics gives an extra card play at the end of each turn, and reaching it raises Escalation. Quantum Computing makes SAE pick its opening card first, where you can see it, and moves the score 1 your way at each era's end. The first side to reach each step gets +1 on its next tech race draw.

steps.say: Your last play before Era 1 scores: look for regions where you are close to present or ahead.

say: Era 1 is over, and every region scores in turn. In each region a side scores only its highest level: present (it controls at least one country), ahead (more countries and more battlegrounds than its rival), or every battleground. Each battleground controlled adds 1. The score track moves by the difference.

You win at once by reaching your end of the track. Otherwise, after 2025 scores, the side the track leans towards wins. If it's even, the side ahead on the tech race wins, and if that's even too, it's a draw. The track started 7 steps towards SAE.

LIO's ability, Resilient institutions: the first time each turn a draw from your own deck shows a 1, it is set aside and you draw again. SAE's ability, Unified command: after SAE plays its own card for its event, its next card played for points that turn counts 1 more.
That's the coaching. From here it's a normal game.

asides.say: Resilient institutions set your 1 aside, and you drew again. Chapter 7 explains.
Unified command: SAE's card played for points counted 1 more. Chapter 7 explains.
